problems.title: Choose a quadratic’s minimum
problems.question: For what a does y=x²-8x+a have minimum value 3?
problems.idea: Complete the square. The squared part has minimum zero.
steps: The square (x-4)² is nonnegative, and equals zero at x=4.
The minimum value is therefore a-16.
Set a-16=3 to obtain a=19.

problems.title: Lines parallel to a plane through an outside point
problems.question: Point A is outside plane w. How many lines through A are parallel to w?
problems.idea: Through A, draw the plane parallel to w. Every line through A within that plane qualifies.
formulas: Through a point outside a plane there is a unique parallel plane.
A line lying in that parallel plane cannot intersect the original plane.
steps: Let p be the plane through A parallel to w.
Choose any direction in p. The corresponding line through A has no intersection with w, so it is parallel to w.
There are infinitely many directions in a plane. The number of qualifying lines is infinite.

problems.title: Subtract two angles with known trig values
problems.question: Given cos(α+β)=3/5, sinβ=3/5, and 0<α,β<π/2, find sinα.
problems.idea: Determine the positive sine of α+β, then use the sine subtraction formula.
formulas: sin(u-v)=sin u cos v-cos u sin v.
steps: The sum α+β lies between 0 and π. Its cosine is positive, so it lies in the first quadrant and sin(α+β)=4/5.
Because β is acute, cosβ=4/5.
problems.note: None of the printed choices equals 7/25. In particular, the choice 3/25 does not follow from the stated data.

problems.title: Reduce a large angle before taking sine
problems.question: Simplify sin(-11π/2+α).
problems.idea: Add a whole number of full turns to the angle.
steps: Add 6π to -11π/2+α to get π/2+α.
Sine is unchanged by three full turns.
Therefore the expression is cosα.

problems.title: Add two exact trigonometric values
problems.question: Find sin(4π/3)+tan(5π/6).
problems.idea: Use reference angles and the signs in quadrants III and II.
steps: Add using denominator 6: -3√3/6-2√3/6=-5√3/6.

problems.title: An angle between two plane projections
problems.question: B,C,D lie in plane w, A is outside it, and AD is perpendicular to w. If AB:AC:AD:BC=5:4:3:√21, find ∠BDC.
problems.idea: First use the two right triangles with vertical side AD, then the cosine rule in BDC.
steps: Scale all lengths by a common t>0. Then BD=√(25-9)t=4t and CD=√(16-9)t=√7t.
The cosine rule gives (16+7-21)/(2·4√7)=1/(4√7).
The common scale cancels, so the angle is uniquely determined by this cosine.

problems.title: Identify skew lines in a cube
problems.question: In cube ABCDA1B1C1D1, P∈AA1, T∈A1B1, K∈B1C1, N∈CC1, M∈DD1, Q∈AD. Which listed line pair is necessarily skew?
problems.idea: The intended pair TP,MQ lies in two adjacent face planes but meets their common edge at different places.
formulas: Skew lines are nonparallel lines that do not intersect.
steps: For interior edge points, write P=(0,0,p), T=(t,0,1), M=(0,1,m), Q=(0,q,0), with all four parameters between 0 and 1.
TP lies in face plane y=0; MQ lies in face plane x=0. Any intersection would have to lie on their shared line x=y=0.
TP meets that line at P, height p>0. Extending MQ to y=0 gives height -mq/(1-q)<0. These are different points, so the lines do not meet.
TP has a nonzero x-direction component; MQ has x-component zero. Thus they are not parallel and are skew.
problems.answer: TP and MQ (option ე), for interior edge points.
problems.note: The usual interior-point convention is needed here. If endpoints are allowed, choosing P=Q=A makes the lines intersect, so “necessarily” would fail without that convention.

problems.title: Count positive trigonometric numbers
problems.question: How many are positive: sin(11π/5), cos(-7π/4), tan(22π/7), cot(5π/3), sin(111π/10)?
problems.idea: Reduce each angle by its period and identify its quadrant.
formulas: Sine and cosine have period 2π; tangent has period π.
steps: sin(11π/5)=sin(π/5)>0. Also cos(-7π/4)=cos(π/4)>0.
tan(22π/7)=tan(π/7)>0, since subtracting 3π leaves π/7.
cot(5π/3)<0 because cosine is positive and sine negative.
sin(111π/10)=sin(11π/10)<0. Exactly three of the five numbers are positive.

problems.title: Recover tangent in the third quadrant
problems.question: α∈(π,3π/2) and |sinα|=a. Find tanα.
problems.idea: In quadrant III, both sine and cosine are negative.
steps: The interval implies 0<a<1 and sinα=-a.
The negative cosine is cosα=-√(1-a²).
Divide the two negative values to get a/√(1-a²).

problems.title: Order sine and cosine without decimal values
problems.question: Let a=sin40°, b=cos40°, c=sin47°. Put them in increasing order.
problems.idea: Express cosine as the sine of a complementary angle.
formulas: Sine is strictly increasing for angles from 0° to 90°.
steps: b=sin50°.
The angles satisfy 40°<47°<50°.
All are in the interval where sine increases. Therefore sin40°<sin47°<sin50°.

problems.title: Distance to a plane: a printed point-name conflict
problems.question: The printed question says C lies in plane w, A lies outside it, C is on AB, AC:BC=2:3, and A is 10 units from w. It then asks for C’s distance to w.
problems.idea: A point explicitly lying in a plane has distance zero. Also check the likely intended version against the answer choices.
formulas: A point in a plane has perpendicular distance 0 from it.
Along a segment ending in a plane, signed perpendicular height varies linearly.
steps: Taken literally, C∈w immediately gives distance(C,w)=0. The other lengths do not change this fact.
No printed choice is zero. If the first sentence intended B∈w instead, then C lies 2/5 of the way from A to B.
Under that corrected reading, the remaining height is (3/5)·10=6.
problems.answer: Literal question: 0. Likely intended question with B∈w: 6 (option ბ).
problems.note: The source names C both as the point in the plane and as the point whose distance is requested. The two readings are kept separate rather than silently changing the problem.

problems.title: A projection does not force a triangle’s angle type
problems.question: Triangle BCD lies in plane w. A is outside w and another plane q. Lines AB,AC,AD meet q at B1,C1,D1. Must B1C1D1 be isosceles, right, obtuse, acute, or have angles 30°,80°,70°?
problems.idea: The stated conditions do not constrain the original triangle’s shape.
formulas: Projection from a point between parallel planes is a homothety: it preserves all triangle angles.
steps: The planes are only said to be distinct, so they may be parallel.
Choose parallel planes w,q with A outside both. The projected triangle is then similar to BCD.
Because BCD itself can be an acute scalene triangle, a right triangle, or an obtuse triangle, none of the listed special shapes is forced.
Likewise, its angles need not be 30°,80°,70°.
problems.answer: None of the preceding answers (option ვ).

problems.title: Compare oblique segments between parallel planes
problems.question: A,B lie in plane w and C,D in parallel plane q. AC makes angle α with q and BD makes angle β with q. Find AC:BD.
problems.idea: Each segment has the same perpendicular component: the separation of the two planes.
formulas: If a segment of length L makes angle θ with a plane, its perpendicular component is Lsinθ.
steps: Let the distance between the distinct planes be h.
Then AC·sinα=h and BD·sinβ=h.
Divide AC=h/sinα by BD=h/sinβ.

problems.title: Which sine value is one-half?
problems.question: Which equal 0.5: I sin150°, II sin670°, III sin210°?
problems.idea: Use reference angles and periodicity.
steps: Only the first value is positive one-half.

problems.title: Range of a squared-trig expression
problems.question: Find the range of y=sin²x+2cos²x.
problems.idea: Replace the sine square so the expression depends on one bounded quantity.
steps: y=(1-cos²x)+2cos²x=1+cos²x.
Its least value is 1 when cosx=0; its greatest is 2 when cos²x=1.
Every intermediate cosine-square value is attained, so the range is the full closed interval.

problems.title: Solve a shifted sine equation
problems.question: Which listed x can satisfy sin(x-2)=-1?
problems.idea: Sine is -1 at -π/2 plus a whole number of full turns.
formulas: sin t=-1 exactly when t=-π/2+2kπ, k∈ℤ.
steps: Set x-2=-π/2+2kπ.
Thus x=2-π/2+2kπ.
Taking k=0 gives the listed value 2-π/2. Substitution makes x-2=-π/2 as required.

problems.title: Tangent of an angle sum
problems.question: sinα=3/5 and 0<α<π/2. Find tan(π/4+α).
problems.idea: Find cosα and tanα, then use the tangent addition formula.
formulas: tan(u+v)=(tan u+tan v)/(1-tan u tan v).
steps: Because α is acute, cosα=4/5 and tanα=3/4.
tan(π/4)=1, so the requested tangent is (1+3/4)/(1-3/4).
This is (7/4)/(1/4)=7. The denominator is nonzero.

problems.title: The three-dimensional locus of equal distances
problems.question: A nondegenerate triangle ABC lies in plane w. What is the locus of spatial points X with XA=XB=XC?
problems.idea: The foot of X’s perpendicular projection into w must be the triangle’s circumcentre.
formulas: For projection H of X into w: XA²=XH²+HA², and similarly for B,C.
In a triangle’s plane, its unique point equidistant from all three vertices is the circumcentre O.
steps: Equal distances from X imply HA²=HB²=HC² after subtracting the common XH².
Thus H=O, so X lies on the perpendicular line through O.
Conversely, every point on that line is equally distant from A,B,C by Pythagoras.
problems.answer: A line perpendicular to w through the circumcentre (option ა).

problems.title: Height above a rectangle from two elevation angles
problems.question: S is outside rectangle ABCD’s plane and SA is perpendicular to it. SB makes a 60° angle with the plane, SD a 30° angle, and the rectangle’s perimeter is 16. Find SA.
problems.idea: The in-plane projections of SB and SD are AB and AD.
steps: Let SA=h. The right triangles give AB=h/√3 and AD=√3h.
The perimeter condition gives AB+AD=8, hence 4h/√3=8.
Solve to obtain h=2√3.

problems.title: Simplify with a tangent identity
problems.question: For cosx≠0, simplify 1/(tan²x+1)+sin²x+cosx·tanx+sinx.
problems.idea: Turn the reciprocal tangent expression into cos²x and the product into sinx.
steps: The first term equals cos²x. The third term equals sinx because cosx is nonzero.
The whole expression becomes cos²x+sin²x+sinx+sinx.
Combine to obtain 1+2sinx.

problems.title: Scale work by people and time
problems.question: Four operators type four pages in four minutes. How many pages can ten operators type in ten minutes?
problems.idea: Assume everyone types at the same constant rate. Divide by the original operator-minutes.
steps: The original work used 4·4=16 operator-minutes.
The rate is 4/16=1/4 page per operator-minute.
Ten operators in ten minutes provide 100 operator-minutes, giving 100/4=25 pages.

problems.title: Distance between equal oblique endpoints
problems.question: A is 2 units above plane w. B,C lie in w, AB=AC=3, and the projections of AB,AC make a 60° angle. Find BC.
problems.idea: Find both projection lengths by Pythagoras, then use the cosine rule.
formulas: If H is A’s foot, HB²=AB²-AH² and HC²=AC²-AH².
steps: Equivalently, HBC is equilateral because two equal sides enclose a 60° angle.

problems.title: Height from equal distances to equilateral vertices
problems.question: An equilateral triangle has side a>0. M is distance b from each vertex. Find M’s perpendicular distance to its plane.
problems.idea: Its projection is the circumcentre, whose distance to a vertex is a/√3.
steps: Equal distances to the three vertices force the projection to the circumcentre O.
The right triangle MOA has hypotenuse b and in-plane leg a/√3.
Thus h²=b²-a²/3. The nonnegative square root is the required distance.
problems.note: If b<a/√3, no such real point M exists. At equality M lies in the triangle’s plane.

problems.title: Compare tangent values given in radians
problems.question: Let a=tan1, b=1, c=tan2. Put them in increasing order.
problems.idea: Unmarked angles are in radians. Place 1 and 2 relative to π/4 and π/2.
formulas: Tangent is negative in quadrant II.
steps: Because π/4<1<π/2, tan1>1.
Because π/2<2<π, tan2<0.
Therefore tan2<1<tan1.

problems.title: When a product of sine and cosine is positive
problems.question: In which quadrants is sinx·cosx positive?
problems.idea: A product is positive when its two nonzero factors have the same sign.
formulas: Quadrant signs (sin,cos): I (+,+), II (+,-), III (-,-), IV (-,+).
steps: The product is positive in quadrant I because both factors are positive.
It is also positive in quadrant III because both factors are negative.
In quadrants II and IV it is negative. On an axis it is zero, so axes are excluded.
